newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares close firm in brisk trade.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares close firm in brisk trade.

text.p: Bucking Wall Street's slide, Chilean blue chips closed higher in strong trade, but with the mood remaining cautious as investors look to Friday's release of the latest U.S. employment figures, said traders.

"I don't see much buying force and some stocks which have risen recently could suffer profit-taking," said Pedro Santa Maria at brokerage Socimer. "Investors will also be keeping a close eye on how interest rates react to the U.S jobs data."
The selective IPSA index ended up 0.57 percent at 96.6 points. The general IGPA index gained 0.62 percent to 5,326.04 points. Turnover was 13 billion pesos.
Traders said the market rose on bargain-hunting and speculation that the Central Bank could ease its credit squeeze before the end of the year.
"People are hoping that there could be a surprise loosening of rates before the year is over," said one dealer.

Traders noted heavy trading in power stocks, including investment companies associated with power utility Enersis on speculation the firm is in talks to sell part of its stake in Endesa to Spanish utility Endesa.
"The market still believes the rumor, even though it has been denied by Enersis," said one dealer.
Enersis closed up 0.2 percent at 252-1/2 pesos while Endesa rose 0.1 percent to 257-1/4 pesos.
Losers included generator Edelnor on fears the company's earnings from its coal-fired Mejillones plant will be hurt by plans to build lower cost natural gas projects in northern Chile, said dealers.
Other decliners included pension fund manager Provida, down 1.1 percent at 9,000 pesos, and steel maker Cap, which fell 1.17 percent to 1,270 pesos.
